body:
Note from the review of PR #1575 (#1556), for this issue's design:

A project saved before #1575 keeps each operation's cached path and its stamp (`project/entity.rs`, `OperationDto { stamp, cache }`). The stamp is a digest of params and geometry with no generator version in it, so a saved Bore op holding a hole wider than the ride clears (e.g. a Ø74.3 bore with a 4 mm end mill) opens fresh and can still post the cored path without regenerating - and verify says ok, which is this issue.

A cheap check that closes that route without the general freed-piece law: at verify time, judge each Bore op's stored holes with the kernel's own verdict, `machining2d::bore_leaves_core(radius, tool_diameter, corner_r, stock_to_leave, through.then_some(THROUGH_CLEAR))` (the same call generate's door and Detect holes make since #1575), and report a finding for any hole it refuses. The same idea applies to any future refusal door whose cached path predates it.
